title: Maximum modulus principle
section: Complex Variables ▷ Theorems Concerning Analytic Functions
terms: maximum modulus principle; maximum principle; boundary maximum; minimum modu- lus principle.

exposition.text:
A nonconstant holomorphic function on a connected open set has no interior local maximum
of its modulus. If it is continuous on the closure of a bounded domain, compactness ensures a
maximum exists and the maximum is attained on the boundary. Continuity on the closure is
essential for this boundary assertion.
If a holomorphic function has no zeros, apply the maximum principle to its reciprocal to obtain
a minimum modulus principle. A function may have an interior minimum of modulus at a
zero. The principle constrains modulus, rather than the complex value itself, because complex
numbers have no compatible ordering.

question.text:
A function f is holomorphic near the closed unit disk, has no zeros there, and satisfies |f(z)| =
1 for |z| = 1. Which must hold?
(A) f(z) = z.
(B) f is constant of modulus 1 on the unit disk.
(C) |f (0)| < 1.
(D) f has a pole outside the disk.
′
(E) f (0) ̸= 0.

solution.text:
Apply the maximum principle to f to obtain |f | ≤ 1 inside. Apply it to the holomorphic re-
ciprocal to obtain 1/|f | ≤ 1. Thus |f | = 1 throughout the disk, and an interior maximum
forces constancy on this connected disk.

question.text:
A function is analytic on a neighborhood of the closed unit disk, has |f | ≤ 1 on its boundary,
and satisfies f(1/2) = 1. What follows?
(A) f has exactly one zero.
(B) f(z) = z on the disk.
(C) f may be any finite Blaschke product.
(D) The hypotheses are inconsistent.
(E) f ≡ 1 on the disk.

solution.text:
The maximum modulus principle first gives |f| ≤ 1 throughout the disk. Equality at an in-
terior point forces f to be constant, and the stated value makes the constant one.

question.text:
A zero-free function f is analytic on a neighborhood of the closed unit disk and satisfies
|f(z)| ≥ 2 on the unit circle. Which conclusion follows?
(A) f is constant.
(B) |f (z)| ≤ 2 throughout the disk.
(C) f(0) = 2
′
(D) f (0) = 0
(E) |f (z)| ≥ 2 throughout the disk.

solution.text:
The reciprocal 1/f is analytic on the disk and has modulus at most 1/2 on the boundary.
The maximum modulus principle gives the same bound inside, hence |f| ≥ 2. The zero-free
hypothesis is essential.
